signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Hike Speculation
signals.text: The G10 scorecard shows JPY leading with an average weekly gain of +1.310% across 7 pairs while SEK lags at -1.378% across 2 pairs, generating a wide bilateral spread of 2.688%. BoJ holds at 1.0%. JPY strength dominates despite its nominal carry deficit, reinforced by strong positive Japanese economic surprises at an ESI index of +23.8 versus Sweden at -6.7. This policy convergence theme and broad cross-asset re-pricing fuel sustained JPY outperformance against low-yielding European peers. Technical positioning remains firmly bearish for JPY crosses as risk sentiment wavers. Trade bias: Bullish JPY/SEK; persistent outperformance spread favors continuation. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — rate hike decision. Risk: BoJ holds rates at 1.00% without hawkish guidance, sharply compressing the bilateral spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Hedging + Unwind Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.17, breaking cleanly below its SMA20 at 157.91, SMA50 at 159.85, and SMA200 at 158.42. The 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal prints a sharp put skew of -2.04 with options implied volatility at 9.7% against HV30 at 10.2% yielding a negative volatility risk premium of -0.6%. BoJ holds at 1.0%. While Fed SOFR at 3.64% vs BoJ TONA at 0.98% maintains a +266bp carry advantage for USD, institutional options demand aggressively buys downside insurance against a crowded carry trade. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; crowded speculative short unwinds threaten deeper pullbacks. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US Core CPI prints well above the 0.2% monthly forecast, reviving broad USD yields.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Vol + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7175, testing its SMA20 at 0.7164 while holding above the SMA50 at 0.7065 and SMA200 at 0.7001. CFTC leveraged fund positioning shows a crowded net long of +50,250 contracts in the 94th percentile of the 52-week range (z = +1.79), contrasting sharply with retail positioning showing an extreme 91% short skew. Options implied volatility sits at 7.0% against HV30 of 5.7% (VRP +1.3%), while the 25-delta risk reversal reflects a mild put skew of -0.55. Although the RBA at 4.35% provides a 60bp carry advantage over the Fed at 3.75% (AONIA vs SOFR differential at -71bp), stalling institutional accumulation indicates upside momentum is tiring. The extreme institutional-retail divergence signals elevated squeeze vulnerability in both directions. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; retail short capitulation risk supports the trend despite crowded spec longs. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US headline inflation accelerates sharply, driving a bear steepener across the US curve.
